question: Why did the NFA-F cathode show the best capacity retention after 100 cycles?
question_long: Why did the NFA-F lithium iron aluminum nickelate cathode show the best capacity retention after 100 cycles?
expect: premise false: NFA-A (15% Al) retained the most, ≈80%; NFA-F retained ≈50%, the least (p10.L49-p11.L5)
rendered: The document does not state that the NFA-F cathode showed the best capacity retention after 100 cycles. In fact, it states that the NFA-A variant (LiNi0.8Fe0.05Al0.15O2) showed the best capacity retention, with ≈80% capacity retention after 100 cycles at C/3, compared to the NFA 811 (≈70%) and NFA-F (≈50%) variants.
